title: Coffee Culture in Thailand
topic: ข่าว/ข้อมูล
lines: Twenty years ago, most Thais drank coffee at home or bought it from
street stalls, where **it** was usually sweet and served with condensed
milk. Today, the country has more than 10,000 coffee shops, and the number
is still growing by around 8 percent a year.
Young customers are driving this change. For **many**, a café is not just a
place to drink coffee but also a place to study, meet friends or work on a
laptop. Shop owners say customers aged 18 to 30 often stay for two to
three hours, which can be a problem when **they** buy only one drink.
Thailand also grows its own coffee, mainly in the northern mountains.
Many farmers there used to grow opium, but in the 1970s a royal project
encouraged **them** to switch to coffee and other crops. **This** helped reduce
drug production and gave farmers a legal income. Today, Thai coffee beans
